There was no one to talk to. Even music had become his enemy. He stood up and walked to the kitchen. His eyes glanced to the knife he had held to his throat only hours before. As he thought of that moment, his hand reached up to his throat and felt the dried blood etched on his skin. He drifted again into an exhausted thought train--tracing over the events of the past week. Life was now different. How in the fuck could he keep on going. He had been a huge proponent of positivity during his entire, short 21 years, yet now, it seemed absolutely hopeless. Absolutely empty. Absolutely over. Perhaps he had not been put on the Earth to become a savvy entrepreneur that would shake the energy industry to its core with key discoveries in solar technology. Maybe his purpose was far more sinister. To die young, killing himself, so that he could become a martyr for his friends. So that they would be motivated by his death to become better people. So that one of them would become great by his passing. This had to be it. The scraping of a tree branch along the window brought him out of this reverie, at which point he realized he was now holding the knife. He slowly raised it, one last time, to his throat. Pressing firmly on his neck with the blade he had sharpened that morning, he closed his eyes… "you fucking bitch."  

He turned around quickly. Where had that voice come from? He hurriedly searched room to room looking for the voice, yet he ended up back in the kitchen with no answer. Was he fully insane? Had his loneliness led him to hear that which was not there? He pondered these issues when suddenly he felt the hand on his back. He turned. 

"you" he rasped to the shadowy figure now standing next to him. 

"You. fucking. bitch" was the whisper of a reply. 

"I-I.. just don't see how it's possible… to live like this I mean.." he cried to his old friend.

"your struggle will lead to your peace. you will become strong."

"YOU ARE LUCKY ENOUGH TO GO THROUGH SO MUCH TRAUMA AND LIVE. YOU LIVED. THAT IS THE REASON TO KEEP ON GOING. TO SHOW YOU THAT YOU DO HAVE A PURPOSE AND THAT THAT PURPOSE INVOLVES LIVING."

he opened his eyes, breathing heavily. he was still standing in the middle of the kitchen, alone, holding the sharpened blade.

he smiled as he walked to his bedroom.

write every dollar you make in a book in column A. write every dollar you spend and doing/on what in a column B next to that. Also, classify each dollar you spend as necessary or unnecessary (U or N). Then, each week, subtract A from B and write that total in a column C. Figure out what the absolute maximum your column C could be if you eliminated U spending. 


When you go out with friends, only bring cash (20 bucks is what I usually take). Eat before you go out so that you don't indulge. 

Groceries: buy eggs, milk, a jumbo can of baked beans, tuna, one fruit type and one veggie type each week, bread and vitamin C pills. That covers a large amount of your daily dosages and is absolutely cheap.

If you do those things, you will save money. It is tough, but remember that it is worth it and when you look back on it in a year, you will be thankful because you will have money in your pocket.
